_about: Editorial flags for images that show how power wanted to be seen (propaganda, official art, posed photographs). Flagging is a classification, not new history: each flag cites the knowledge-base text that justifies it. The note shown on the site is the image's own caption plus the checklist in sources/primary_sources.md ('How to read primary sources critically'). Traced in CONTENT_TRACE.md §1 (id I1).
basis: images/IMAGE_INDEX.md, 'How images were chosen': "Propaganda (the Völkischer Beobachter, Hitler Youth marches), official art (Bürde, Hünten) and posed colonial photographs show how power wanted to be seen — read them with the same source criticism as texts."

kaiserproklamation.why: Bürde is named as official art in IMAGE_INDEX.md 'How images were chosen'; the brief names 'Bürde's celebration of the new emperor'.

koeniggraetz.why: Hünten is named as official art in IMAGE_INDEX.md 'How images were chosen'.

kolonialbeamter.why: 'Posed colonial photographs' in IMAGE_INDEX.md 'How images were chosen'; the brief names 'the posed colonial photo'.

hj-march.why: 'Hitler Youth marches' are named as propaganda in IMAGE_INDEX.md 'How images were chosen'; the index title is 'Hitler Youth propaganda march'.

vb-enabling.why: 'the Völkischer Beobachter' is named as propaganda in IMAGE_INDEX.md 'How images were chosen'; the caption calls it 'The Nazi party paper celebrating the Enabling Act'.

openQuestions: Not flagged without the owner's decision (official messaging of other states, not named in IMAGE_INDEX.md): white-rose (RAF leaflet drop), hakenkreuz (US Army newsreel), wir-bleiben (West German government poster).
